findings.title: Fallback to all-clients resource can throw NullPointerException
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no resource exists for the specific client, the code loads the all-clients resource via getResourceTypeResource() and immediately passes it to policyStore.findByResource(server, resource) and later to new ResourcePermission(resource, ...). getResourceTypeResource() can return null (e.g. the Clients type resource is absent for a resource server created before this type existed, or was not initialized), so the permission check throws an NPE/500 instead of safely returning false.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission returns the all-clients sentinel instead of client ids
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission iterates every resource of type Clients, including the type-level resource whose name is literally "Clients", and adds resource.getName() to the result. Callers expect the set to contain client ids (specific-client resources are named by client id), so a grant on all clients contributes the useless entry "Clients" and does not expand to the ids of clients that have no individual resource. Filtering by this set therefore misses clients covered only by an all-clients permission.

findings.title: getResourceName has no Clients branch
findings.body: getResourceName only special-cases the Users resource type: it returns "All users" for the type resource and the username for a user resource, otherwise falling back to resource.getDisplayName(). Client resources created by this PR are named by client id and have no display name set, so representations of Clients permissions/resources will show a null/empty name instead of "All clients" or the client's clientId, unlike Users.

findings.title: Client-removed listener can call unsupported V2 setPermissionsEnabled when both FGAP features are enabled
findings.body: The listener now runs when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (v1) is enabled, but AdminPermissions.management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2 whenever ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is also enabled, and MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2 whose setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) throws UnsupportedOperationException. With both features enabled, deleting a client fires ClientRemovedEvent and this call throws, potentially failing the client-deletion operation instead of being a no-op in V2.
